name: Long Strip
summary: Buy two puts and one call at the same ATM strike and expiry; the mirror of the strap -- long volatility with a bearish tilt.

legs.strike_rule: ATM strike, put delta closest to -0.50.
Same ATM strike as the puts.

max_profit: downside: (2 * strike * 100) - debit as the underlying approaches zero; upside: unlimited but at half the slope
max_loss: net debit paid, if the underlying finishes exactly at the strike
breakevens: downside: strike - debit/(2*100) per share; upside: strike + debit/100 per share

greeks.delta: negative, roughly -0.50 per unit at entry

when_to_use: You expect a large move and believe down is more likely, with IV cheap. Fits pre-earnings on a crowded long name, or ahead of a macro print in a fragile tape. Note the structural headwind: equity put skew means the two puts are the expensive legs, so this is more costly than a strap on the same name.
entry_rules: IV rank <= 25 -- and check skew: if 25-delta put IV exceeds 25-delta call IV by more than 6 vol points, the puts are already crowded and the edge is gone.
Ratio exactly 2 puts : 1 call (GCD = 1; all legs long, so Alpaca accepts the MLeg).
Downside breakeven distance <= 0.75 * the average absolute adverse move on comparable catalysts.
DTE extends >= 5 days past the catalyst.
OI >= 500 per contract, bid/ask <= 8% of mid.
management_rules: Close within 30 minutes of a scheduled event print.
If the underlying breaks down and net delta exceeds -1.20 per unit, sell one put to bank the directional move and leave a straddle running.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
No short legs, so no assignment risk. All legs are long, so ITM legs auto-exercise at expiry into up to 200 short shares (puts) or 100 long shares (call) per unit. Close everything before 15:45 ET.
assignment_risk: None from short legs. The only stock-delivery path is OCC auto-exercise of your own ITM long legs at expiry, prevented by the 15:45 ET close.
liquidity_needs: ATM strikes; OI >= 500; route as one package.
common_mistakes: Ignoring put skew, which makes the strip structurally pricier than the strap; expecting symmetric breakevens; holding past the catalyst into vol crush.
zero_dte_notes: Same objection as the strap -- 1.5x the theta of a 0DTE straddle. Only around scheduled prints, and a plain 0DTE put usually expresses the view more cheaply.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
